steps.title: Retain the same actual laws, operators and original inputs
steps.text: Apply the independently accepted actual projected-rotation parent with the six original analytic caller conditions. Extract its same twelve witnesses, actual conditional components and mean preservation. Identify the inherited complete centered and conditional-mean-zero Hilbert spaces explicitly; the typed change only exposes the parent proposition and introduces no assumption.

steps.title: Test the square identity and cancel mixed terms
steps.text: Positivity gives selfadjoint Γ_0. Test A_0²+Γ_0²=I against u, moving each selfadjoint operator through the inner product, to obtain the norm identity. Move A_0 and Γ_0 through the mixed product and use their commutation to obtain the cross-term identity. These identities hold on the full centered Hilbert space, including the zero space.

steps.title: Derive the corrector operator identities from the same inverse
steps.text: Set K=A_0 Inv. Evaluate both sides of Inv Γ_0=Γ_0 Inv=I and of the two commutation identities. Consequently KΓ_0=Γ_0K=A_0 and KA_0=A_0K. The inverse remains on H_P^0; it is never extended to constants or assumed to be a new caller certificate.

steps.title: Reduce the remaining mixed inner product
steps.text: Apply A_0²+Γ_0²=I to u. Commutation and KΓ_0=A_0 give A_0 K A_0 u+Γ_0 A_0u=K(A_0²u+Γ_0²u)=Ku. Test against v and use selfadjoint A_0 and Γ_0. This is precisely the mixed term needed for the corrector expansion.

steps.title: Evaluate both diagonal terms and align the mixed terms
steps.text: Move Γ_0 across the first diagonal inner product, use Γ_0K=A_0, and move A_0 across once more. For the other diagonal use KΓ_0=A_0 directly. Real symmetry and the preceding cross-term identity align the two mixed products without any surjectivity or dimension argument.

steps.title: Expand the corrector and compute its exact change
steps.text: Write X=||A_0u||²,Y=||Γ_0u||²,Z=||A_0v||²,W=||Γ_0v||²,t=⟨A_0u,Γ_0v⟩ and r=⟨Ku,v⟩. For u′=A_0u−Γ_0v and v′=Γ_0u+A_0v, norm expansion gives ||u′||²=X+W−2t and ||v′||²=Y+Z+2t. The diagonal and mixed identities give ⟨Ku′,v′⟩=X−Z+r−2t. Hence C(u′,v′)=(−X−Y+Z+W)/2−r=−||u||²/2+||v||²/2−r. Subtract C(u,v)=(||u||²−||v||²)/2−r. All cross terms cancel and the exact half and signs remain.

steps.title: Substitute the actual conditional and polar components
steps.text: For arbitrary actual f with integral zero, use the parent to produce its actual f_P and the actual conditional g_P of the same g. Keep f_V=V_0*Rf and g_V=V_0*Rg. Apply the two-argument congruence of C to the already proved component formulas, then subtract C(f_P,f_V) and apply the preceding algebra with u=f_P,v=f_V. Thus the corrector is evaluated on actual components, rather than components defined by the rotation right-hand sides.

steps.title: Reassemble every original clause with the same witnesses
steps.text: Retain the full-micro intertwining identity, actual projected rotation, pair energy and all earlier law/kernel/root/inverse/polar conclusions, and adjoin only the new corrector identity. This supplies the discrete corrector-change ingredient for the first two signed terms of B4/B28. Time evolution, the weak H1 bridge, nonexplosion, implementation error and expected-cost composition are not inferred from this algebra.
